> This PR seems to have include all commits from a pull-request of mine which has been merged previously. Not sure why, if anybody thinks they know please let me know.

It looks like you opened your pull request from `master`. It's advisable to start each new pull request from a new branch, and that (when you start working on it) that branch be synced up with `upstream master`.

See [creating a branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/development/contributing.html#creating-a-branch)

With how your branch is now, if you don't want your old commits, I think you'd have to do something like (assuming `upstream` is `https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas`)
```bash
git fetch upstream master
git rebase -i upstream/master
```
and then drop the commits from your previous pull request. Once that's done, you'd have to do a forced push.
Thanks @MarcoGorelli I will make sure to start a new branch next time before submitting a PR.

review_comments: you can use contextlib.suppress here to make this much easier to read
Wasn't sure what to do here

I think the suggestion is to use `contextlib.suppress` to ignore the error.

e.g. if you were running `1/0`, you would do
```python
In [1]: from contextlib import suppress

In [2]: with suppress(ZeroDivisionError):
   ...:     1/0
   ...:

```
instead of
```python
In [3]: try:
   ...:     1/0
   ...: except ZeroDivisionError:
   ...:     pass
   ...:

```

So the suggestion is to use contextlib.suppress in order to change the following lines of code. Im not sure exactly how to do so given that the code being tested here is a context manager itself

```
            try:
                with HDFStore(path) as tbl:
                    raise ValueError("blah")
            except ValueError:

```
